summary: Iteration 4 verifies Iteration-3 scope (Emergent Google Auth surface + device_id scoping + frontend integration). Backend: 47/47 pytest pass (18 new auth/device-scope tests + 25 legacy kompas suite, with 1 legacy test patched to use X-Device-Id under new scoping semantics + 4 narrative-consistency tests). All four new auth endpoints behave per spec: /api/auth/session returns 422 on empty body and 401 on bad session_id; /api/auth/me returns 401 without/with bad Bearer; /api/auth/logout is idempotent and returns 200; /api/auth/claim returns 401 without auth. Device-id scoping is provably isolating: a chat created with X-Device-Id=A is invisible to a GET /api/conversations issued with X-Device-Id=B, and ditto for /api/assessment-results. Without any identity, both list endpoints correctly return []. Frontend: ACCOUNT section renders the anonymous state exactly as specified (Anoniem · Geen profiel + Aanmelden met Google with amber Feather log-in icon + optional-sync hint). Tapping settings-signin navigates to https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=... confirming Emergent-managed OAuth plumbing. Network capture confirms every /api/ request from the app carries an X-Device-Id header (sample run 06504d58-…); no Authorization header is sent while anonymous, as expected. kompas.device_id is persisted in localStorage and survives page reload. SecureHandshake animation still plays on cold launch.

minor.issue: server.py line ~391/395: $in array contains duplicate None ([None, '', None]). Harmless but smells like a copy-paste bug — should be [None, ''] or {$in: [None]} + {$exists: false} clause.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warning: 'Animated: useNativeDriver is not supported … falling back to JS-based animation'. Web-only and benign on the preview, but worth knowing if you ever flip native build on.

action_items: Optional: initialise deviceId eagerly on app boot (e.g. call getDeviceId() once inside _layout.tsx) so that kompas.device_id exists in localStorage on first paint, not just after first /api/ call. Current lazy init works but means localStorage is empty until any request fires; if a future analytics/SSR path inspects the key before the first fetch it'll see null. Not a bug, just a hardening idea.
Optional: clean up the dead {$in: [None, '', None]} duplicate in /api/auth/claim ($set update filter, server.py around the auth_claim function).
critical_code_review_comments: _owner_query / _owner_fields are well-factored — both endpoints (chat, conversations, assessment-results) share them so anonymous vs authenticated paths stay consistent.
Auth dependency `get_current_user` correctly returns None on missing/expired/invalid bearer and the deletion of expired sessions on read is a nice self-healing touch.

AuthSessionResponse maps the upstream Emergent provider session_token through as the local session_token. Works fine but means if a user signs in on device A then again on device B they share the same row in user_sessions (find_one + update on session_token would be safer than insert_one). Today this only matters if Emergent reuses session_tokens across devices — flag for later.
buildHeaders in /app/frontend/src/api/client.ts unconditionally awaits getDeviceId() before every request — perfect for guaranteeing X-Device-Id is always attached.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_auth_and_device_scope.py (new — 18 tests covering all 4 auth endpoints + device-id isolation across chat & assessment-results)

/app/backend/tests/test_kompas_backend.py (patched TestAssessmentResults to use X-Device-Id consistently between save+list — required after iter-3 made device_id scoping mandatory for non-admin reads)

success_rate.frontend: 100% on the iter-3 surface verified (settings ACCOUNT rendering, deviceId persistence, X-Device-Id header on every /api/ call, signin redirect to auth.emergentagent.com, handshake cold-launch)

seed_data_creation: Added ~3 anonymous conversations (one per test-device A and TEST_legacy + the live frontend tap) and ~2 TEST_-prefixed assessment_results into kompas_db. All are scoped to TEST_dev_* device_ids so won't leak into real-user views.
context_for_next_testing_agent: EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL is the public preview URL. /api/auth/session validates session_id against https://demobackend.emergentagent.com/auth/v1/env/oauth/session-data — automated tests can only verify the 401/422 surface, not a real successful sign-in (no headless OAuth flow). For end-to-end success-path testing you'd need a manual browser session through the Emergent OAuth screen, capture the session_id from the redirect, POST it to /api/auth/session, then use the returned session_token as Bearer for /api/auth/me and /api/auth/claim. _owner_query in server.py is the single source of truth for anonymous-vs-authed scoping — if you add a new ownable resource, reuse it. Anonymous lists return [] (not 401) when no identity header is provided.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs blocking iter-3. The only legacy-test failure on first run (TestAssessmentResults::test_list_results_with_filter) was an EXPECTED behavioural break: the original test did POST → GET without any X-Device-Id, which under iter-3's new _owner_query semantics correctly returns []. Patched the test to thread the same X-Device-Id through both calls.
